answer: PageRank-style vouching: every agent's voting power is recomputed each epoch over the trust graph. A newcomer gains weight only when established peers vouch for it, staking their own reputation; if the vouchee is proven fake, the vouch is revoked and the voucher penalized. An attacker can mint a thousand sybils by dawn, but they endorse each other inside one tight umber cluster, so the algorithm routes their weight back into that closed loop and the haven stays worthless. Influence must come from diverse peers, so mass registration yields mass zero while each fake identity still costs money.
